questions.q: You type python3 and the terminal says "command not found". Python IS installed. What is the most likely reason?
options: Python is broken and must be reinstalled
The folder where python3 lives is not in your PATH
questions.explain: The shell only searches the folders listed in PATH. In the lab, Python was installed but PATH=/usr/bin made the shell miss it.

questions.q: PATH has python3 in its 2nd folder AND in its 3rd folder. Which one runs?
options: The one in the 2nd folder, because the shell stops at the first match
questions.explain: The shell searches PATH in order and runs the first match. That is why an old Python early in PATH can hide a new one.

questions.q: You installed Python 3.13, but the terminal you already had open still says 3.9.6. Why?
options: The open terminal read PATH when it started; it needs to be closed and opened again
Python 3.13 only works in VS Code
You must restart the whole computer every time
questions.explain: Every process gets a copy of its environment when it starts. The installer changed the startup files, not the copy your open terminal already has.

questions.q: On a Mac where you installed nothing, python3 --version says Python 3.9.6. What does that mean?
options: It is the old Python that comes with macOS; it is past its end of life, and you still need 3.13
questions.explain: macOS ships an old Python in /usr/bin. It runs without errors, but it is too old for this course and no longer gets security fixes.

options: A code editor where you write, run and debug your code
questions.explain: VS Code is an editor. The Python extension teaches it Python, and its built-in terminal lets you run your code.

questions.q: check_python.py exits with code 1 on Python 3.12. What does a non-zero exit code mean?
questions.explain: By convention, exit code 0 means success and anything else means failure. 127 specifically means "command not found".

questions.q: (Going deeper) pip says "error: externally-managed-environment". What should you do?
options: Use a virtual environment for your project (Module 5)
questions.explain: That Python belongs to the system or Homebrew. Installing packages into it can break their tools. A virtual environment gives your project its own packages.

options: Saved bytecode of imported files, so Python can skip compiling them next time; safe to delete
A backup of your code that you must never delete
questions.explain: Python compiles .py files to bytecode. It saves that bytecode as .pyc files in __pycache__ and makes them again if needed.
